messages:
Anya: quick heads-up — just finished a side-by-side run of rw-13b-v1 across SXM (nvlink-enabled) and PCIe nodes in us-west. seeing consistent p95 delta and a small quality blip with q4. anyone else?
Ravi: which instance types + kernels?
Anya: SXM = a100-sxm-80 + runtime kernel v2.3.1, PCIe = a100-pcie + runtime v2.3.1 (same runtime), kernels: custom attention kernels on SXM, fallback kernels on PCIe. batch=1, seq=1024, kv cache warm.
Kevin: numbers?
Anya: median latency SXM 38ms, PCIe 58ms. p95 SXM 62ms, PCIe 112ms. throughput (tokens/s) SXM ~340, PCIe ~210 for the same config.
Leah: curious if NVLink p2p is actually used — did you verify peer-to-peer and probe topology?
Anya: yep ran nvlink topo and confirmed links. also observed that when we don't pin processes to NUMA nodes on PCIe boxes, p95 balloons. numactl pin helped a lot.
Ravi: can you paste the numactl line you used?
Anya: sure — run like:
```
numactl --physcpubind=+0-23 --membind=0 
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python bench_infer.py --model rw-13b-v1 --batch 1 --seq 1024
```
Leah: that reduced PCIe p95 by ~10-15%?
Anya: exactly. with pinning PCIe p95 dropped from 112ms -> ~95ms, throughput up ~8%. still behind SXM though.
Kevin: what about quantization? you mentioned q4 quality blip.
Anya: ran q4 and q2 modes. q4 latency improves 18% but on our long-form eval set (>=1500 tokens) we see a 0.7% BLEU/EM-equivalent drop and occasional trailing hallucination. q2 gave slightly worse quality.
Ravi: do we know if kernel selection interacts with quantization? maybe some fused kernels behave differently on SXM vs fallback on PCIe.
Kevin: yes — our custom fused attention + kv-cache kernel is used on SXM and has quant-aware code paths. fallback kernel on PCIe uses separate matmuls which may accumulate more fp error in q4.
Leah: notes for capacity sizing: if you need sustained 5k tok/s p50 ~25ms, my rough calc: 1 SXM node = ~300 tok/s -> need ~17 nodes; 1 PCIe node = ~200 tok/s -> need ~25 nodes. these are with caching enabled.
Anya: added: cross-region oddity — ran same tests in eu-west on PCIe fleet and p95 was 10-12% higher than us-west. driver version difference + BIOS power profile suspected.
Mike: I can open infra ticket to sync driver/BIOS across regions.
bench-bot: perf-run 1823456789 completed — artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1823456789/artifacts (charts + raw csv) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Ravi: can someone upload the p95 vs batch charts and the kernel-use heatmap? want to see per-layer hotspots.
Kevin: uploaded: /dashboards/eng-ml/1823456789/p95_batch_vs_topo.png and kernel_heatmap_1823456789.png. link in perf artifacts.
Leah: next actions: (1) confirm driver/BIOS parity in eu-west (Mike), (2) test enabling fused kernels on a PCIe canary (Kevin/infra), (3) expand eval set for q4 long-tail prompts and run A/B with fallback decoder (Anya).
Anya: also, add a short log snippet I saw when PCIe fallback used:
```
WARNING: fallback_attention_kernel: using slower matmul path for layer 10
KV cache hits: 98.3%
```
Ravi: let's also try a single-region canary where we force same kernel set on PCIe (if possible) to isolate topology from kernel differences.
Mike: opened INFRA-3247 to track eu-west driver parity and INFRA-3248 for PCIe canary.
Anya: awesome — thanks. I'll kick off expanded q4 eval and share results here when ready. :thumbsup:
